channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Afghan Finance Minister Visits Iran for Economic Discussions
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Finance, Mohammad Nasir Akhund, is in Iran for an official visit at the invitation of Iran's Minister of Agriculture. Discussions will focus on bilateral economic, trade, and customs issues, as well as preparations for a joint economic commission meeting.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches National Cargo Airline, Alatau Air Cargo
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a national cargo airline, Alatau Air Cargo, which plans to expand its fleet to ten aircraft. The airline aims to compete with major international players and is preparing for its first commercial flights in early next year, focusing on securing clients.

item.title: Three-Year-Old Murder Case Solved in Abay Region
item.description: Police in the Abay Region have solved a murder committed over three years ago. The suspect, who was serving time for another crime, confessed to the murder after investigators pursued new leads. The suspect has indicated the location where the victim's body was hidden.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Discuss Border Crossings Using ID Cards
item.description: Diplomats from Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan met in Tashkent to discuss simplifying travel between the two nations. A key topic was the potential for citizens to cross the border using national ID cards instead of passports. The meeting also touched upon employment for Uzbek citizens in Kazakhstan and the QazETA electronic entry system.

item.title: UNHCR Representative Urges Support for Afghanistan for Global Stability
item.description: Arafat Jamal, UNHCR representative in Afghanistan, emphasizes that supporting the country is an investment in global stability, not just humanitarian aid. He urges continued support from South Korea, highlighting Afghanistan's strategic importance and the potential international consequences of neglect. Many returnees face challenges.

item.title: Tashkent Reports 35-Fold Increase in Meningococcal Infections, 24 Deaths
item.description: Tashkent has recorded 354 cases of meningococcal infection in the first nine months of 2026, a 35-fold increase from the previous year, resulting in 24 deaths, mostly children. Health authorities are investigating the surge and implementing preventive measures, including vaccination for contacts.

item.title: AI Developer Anthropic Eyes Up to $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Upcoming IPO
item.description: AI firm Anthropic, creator of the Claude chatbot, is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) with a potential valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. Investors have shown significant demand, with interest reportedly six times the available shares. The company plans to offer 825 million shares at prices between $70 and $78 each, aiming for a total offering of up to $64.4 billion.

item.title: Rehabilitated Power Line in Faryab Province to Benefit 60,000 Consumers
item.description: Afghanistan's Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, inaugurated a rehabilitated 110 kV power transmission line in Faryab province. The project is expected to provide stable electricity to approximately 60,000 consumers, support industrial activities, and contribute to economic and social development. The Islamic Emirate aims to reduce reliance on imported electricity.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways CEO Detained Amid Corruption Investigation
item.description: Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) National Company has stated that its operations continue as normal following the detention of its CEO, Yerzhas Otynshiyev, on suspicion of corruption. The company assured investors, creditors, and partners that all obligations will be met. Information regarding the pre-trial investigation remains confidential as per the Criminal Procedure Code.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Assures Investors of Continued Commitment After Chairman's Detention
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) stated it is operating normally following the detention of its chairman, Yeldjas Otinshev. The company affirmed that all obligations to investors, creditors, and partners remain unchanged. KTZ is cooperating with law enforcement agencies in the ongoing investigation.

item.title: ICC Partially Suspends Afghanistan War Crimes Investigation, Appeals Filed
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has partially suspended its investigation into alleged war crimes in Afghanistan, including those involving US forces and IS-K. The court's prosecution has appealed this decision, while investigations into other alleged crimes in the country will continue separately.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Audit of Cybersecurity Committee Amid Data Leaks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office has initiated a comprehensive audit of the Cybersecurity Committee within the Ministry of Digital Development, following personal data leaks and disruptions to Yandex services. The audit will examine the legality of personal data collection, storage, and transfer, and the protection of citizens' rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan police solve three-year-old murder case in Abai region
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Abai region have solved the murder of a man who disappeared over three years ago. The suspect confessed to the crime and revealed the location where the body was hidden. The case has been sent to court.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways pledges full cooperation with investigation after CEO's detention
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) stated it is fully cooperating with law enforcement in a pre-trial investigation following the detention of its chairman, Yerlan Otynshiyev. The company has no further information beyond public statements and is operating normally.

item.title: Kyrgyz President addresses residents' appeals on property, social, and infrastructure issues
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with residents of Jeti-Oguz and Tong districts, addressing their appeals concerning property rights, social issues, and infrastructure development. He instructed state bodies to ensure fair consideration of all matters raised.

item.title: Taliban Ask Russia to Build Oil Refineries in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghan authorities have invited Russian companies to build oil refineries in the country and increase purchases of Russian petroleum products. They also seek Russian participation in developing raw material fields to balance trade. This comes as Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk visited Kabul with a business delegation, signing 15 memorandums of cooperation worth $103 million.

item.title: Climate Change Leading to Increased Cardiovascular Diseases, Allergies in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Climate change is contributing to a rise in cardiovascular diseases, allergies, and bronchial asthma in Kyrgyzstan, according to Gulbara Ishenapyssova, Deputy Minister of Health. Unusual heat exacerbates existing conditions, particularly affecting the elderly, children, and those with heart problems. Floods and other natural disasters linked to climate change also pose risks to public health and infrastructure.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Top Officials Arrested Amid Corruption Probe; UK Sanctions Russian Firm
item.description: Two top executives from Kazakhstan's quasi-state sector, including the head of Samruk-Kazyna Fund and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, were arrested on corruption charges. Meanwhile, the UK sanctioned Russian company SIBUR, which has stakes in Kazakh projects. President Tokayev called the arrests a 'serious signal' about widespread corruption.

item.title: Tajikistan and Uzbekistan Plan New Joint Ventures for Raw Material Processing
item.description: Tajikistan and Uzbekistan discussed launching new joint ventures and deep processing of raw materials during talks in Dushanbe. The countries aim to create competitive finished products with high added value, moving beyond simple resource supply. They also agreed to exchange experience and combine production capabilities.

item.title: Ariana Afghan Airlines to Launch Direct Flights Between Kandahar and Dubai on November 22
item.description: Ariana Afghan Airlines, operating under Taliban control, has announced the commencement of direct flights between Kandahar and Dubai starting November 22. The airline stated this new route aims to foster trade, investment, and economic ties between the Taliban administration and the UAE. Tickets will be available at Ariana offices and travel agencies.

item.title: President Orders Retrial of Former Police Officer's Case
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered a fair review of a former police officer's case. The officer claims he was unjustly imprisoned for three months while his colleague, who allegedly had connections in the Prosecutor General's Office, was released. The president instructed relevant authorities to thoroughly investigate the incident and ensure a just legal decision.

item.title: Advocating for Women's Rights: A Call to Preserve Dignity and Equality
item.description: The article emphasizes that while political powers change, a nation's strength lies in its people's culture and awareness. It urges society to uphold women's rights as a moral duty, warning against the normalization of injustice and deprivation. True progress requires recognizing women's equal rights to learn, grow, and contribute to the future.

item.title: Uzbekistan Updates Rules for Over-the-Counter Drug Classification
item.description: Uzbekistan has revised requirements for drugs that can be sold without a prescription. The changes, effective in three months, allow drugs safely self-administered without a doctor's supervision to be reclassified. Foreign regulators' experience will also be considered.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliamentarians Inspect Pre-Trial Detention Center, Hear Inmate Complaints
item.description: Members of the Kyrgyz Parliament inspected Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 21, addressing inmate concerns about delayed trials, biased investigations, and inadequate medical care. Deputies urged the center's administration to provide necessary medical examinations for those in need.

item.title: White House Announces Historic Trump-Putin-Xi Meeting at APEC Summit
item.description: The White House has announced a historic three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China. The primary focus will be nuclear arms control, with discussions on a potential new trilateral agreement.

item.title: Tajikistan Villages Explore Biogas from Cow Dung to Replace Firewood
item.description: In Tajikistan, UNDP projects have installed 37 biogas reactors converting cow dung into fuel and fertilizer, reducing greenhouse gas emissions. One family in Kulob reports lower energy costs and improved crop yields due to the biogas system, which also helps conserve land fertility amid climate change.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Investigates Personal Data Protection
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office is conducting an investigation into the protection of personal data within the country. The probe aims to assess the measures in place to safeguard citizens' private information and ensure compliance with data protection laws.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber Uncovers 51 Billion Tenge in Financial Irregularities
item.description: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber has identified financial violations totaling 51 billion tenge and inefficient use of funds amounting to 47 billion tenge. A large-scale audit of the science sector revealed serious shortcomings in the distribution of state funding, implementation of scientific projects, and control over budget expenditures. Despite increased state funding for science, audit results show a significant gap between allocated funds and achieved outcomes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Salary Indexation, Presidential Elections, and Visa-Free Seychelles Travel Discussed
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's latest 'PROsto!' digest covers upcoming salary indexation, presidential election candidates, and visa-free travel to Seychelles. It also details the Social Fund's proposal to use pension savings for housing construction and the findings of an investigation into the death of Amir Kunakov in Ala-Archa National Park, which led to dismissals in the Ministry of Emergency Situations.

item.title: Trump, Putin, Xi to hold first trilateral nuclear arms talks
item.description: US, Chinese, and Russian leaders will discuss nuclear arms reduction for the first time in a trilateral format. Presidents Trump, Xi, and Putin will also address nuclear proliferation and Iran during their meeting in China next week. The talks will occur on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan amends rules allowing officials to earn additional income
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has revised rules for civil servants in political and special positions, allowing them to engage in additional paid activities under certain conditions. These activities include educational, expert, scientific, and creative work, provided they do not affect primary duties or create conflicts of interest. Officials can also engage in public service activities.

item.title: Dozens of archaeological sites damaged in Uzbekistan due to heavy machinery and illegal construction
item.description: Dozens of historical sites in Uzbekistan have been damaged by heavy machinery, agricultural activities, and illegal construction. Investigations revealed damage to 26 archaeological sites and 48 instances of unauthorized construction in their protected zones. Eight criminal cases have been initiated.

item.title: WHO: Diabetes is a major public health problem in Afghanistan
item.description: The World Health Organization has stated that diabetes is a significant public health issue in Afghanistan. Further details on the scope and impact of diabetes in the country were not provided in the source text.

item.title: Tajik migrant needs over 80,000 rubles to start work in Moscow
item.description: A Tajik citizen planning to work in Moscow will need over 80,000 rubles, according to the Ministry of Labor's representative office in Russia. This amount covers document processing, including work permits and medical exams, and initial living expenses. Actual costs may be higher.

item.title: US Flights Grounded Due to Communication System Failure at All Airports
item.description: All flights across the US were halted due to a communication system failure affecting air traffic controllers. Over 1.5 million passengers were impacted as planes were unable to take off for more than four hours. The issue stemmed from an outdated system experiencing technical difficulties.

item.title: Respiratory Infections Surge in Gaza Amid Flooding and Lack of Supplies
item.description: The number of people suffering from respiratory infections is increasing in the Gaza Strip, exacerbated by heavy rains flooding refugee shelters. The World Health Organization reports a significant rise in infections due to overcrowding and damp conditions. A shortage of laboratory equipment and reagents hinders timely diagnosis and treatment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses New EU Carbon Requirements for Metal Exports in Antalya
item.description: Kazakhstan's metal exports to the EU, valued at €611 million in 2025, face new carbon emission requirements starting in 2026. The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) will impose financial obligations based on production emissions. Kazakh exporters are preparing for these changes, discussed at the COP31 climate conference.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Addresses Allegations of Brother's Involvement in Hotel Dispute
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov responded to accusations regarding the "Novel" guesthouse, allegedly linked to his brother. A resident accused state security of seizing his property after a $14 million claim. Japarov denied the claim, accusing the resident of seizing land with criminal groups and Russian investors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Eases Restrictions for Tourism Businesses Near Issyk-Kul Lake
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering easing construction restrictions for tourism facilities near Issyk-Kul Lake. The government may reduce the required setback from the shoreline from 75 to 25 meters, allowing lighter structures for approximately 70-80 families in the area.

item.title: Russia to Increase Taxes for Migrants with Dependents from 2027
item.description: From January 1, 2027, Russia will implement higher tax payments for certain foreign workers with dependent children and family members. The Ministry of Internal Affairs initiated these changes to financially limit migrants from bringing non-working relatives. Additional taxation aims to reduce the burden on the social sphere.
